content:
Reuters reports that a revised draft will extend tax benefits for foreign companies supplying machinery and equipment to Indian contract manufacturers for 10 years. Details below.

Apple is set to receive a major tax break in India

According to the report, India is planning to extend a tax incentive set to expire in 2031 until 2041. The exemption would prevent foreign companies from being taxed in India simply because they own equipment used by Indian contract manufacturers.

Here's what Reuters reports:

None

The news marks a significant win for Apple, which had lobbied hard for the tax break. The incentive was introduced earlier this year and was originally slated to expire in 2031.

The announcement comes weeks after India scrapped import duties of 5% and 7.5% on several components used in the production of smartphones and other electronic devices, further cementing India's role in Apple's efforts to diversify its supply chain away from China.

As cited by Reuters, according to Counterpoint Research, India "will produce 26% of the world's iPhones in 2026, a major jump from 6% four years prior."
